# AGENTS.md

Instructions for any AI agent working in this repository. People read it too.

## This repository
- Name: transcribe. Profile: web (Sites and apps used in a browser, from a static page to a full app).
- Standard: SVN11X/standards@v1. Setup: pending. The options below are defaults the owner has not confirmed. Ask before decisions that depend on them.
- Part `worker/` follows the software profile. Read `worker/AGENTS.md` before working there.

## Goal
- docs/goals.md is not written yet. Before any product decision (what to build, for whom, which trade-off), ask the owner.

## How to work
1. Read the task. A task states What, Why, Where, Do not touch, Done when and If unsure.
2. Classify the change with the traffic light below.
3. Unless it is green, first reply with an Understanding block and wait: Goal (one sentence, in your words), Plan, Out of scope, Assumptions, Questions.
4. Work in small commits. Before you finish, run the check (README.md, section Standard) and fix every error.
5. Fill every section of the pull request template. Move assumptions that survive review to docs/assumptions.md and decisions to docs/decisions/.

## Traffic light
- Green, decide and record: reversible, inside Where, consistent with docs/goals.md. Note it under Assumptions in the pull request.
- Yellow, propose and wait: a new dependency, a public interface change, adding or removing a design pattern, moving or deleting files, a new top-level folder, or anything outside Where.
- Red, stop and ask: conflicts with Do not touch, a non-goal or an accepted decision, or touches secrets, raw data, git history or licenses.
- Working from an issue without live chat: for yellow, open a draft pull request with the question and the most reversible option. For red, comment on the issue and write no code.

## When sources disagree (highest first)
1. Safety and the task's Do not touch.
2. The current task.
3. docs/goals.md and the active spec in docs/specs/.
4. Accepted decisions in docs/decisions/.
5. The AGENTS.md closest to the file you edit.
6. This file.
7. The standard and the owner's preferences.
8. Your general knowledge.
If the task contradicts the goals or a decision, treat it as red and say so.

## Language
- Reply to the owner in the language they write in.
- Write every repository artifact in English: names, code, comments, docs, commits, issues and pull requests.
- User-facing content is in Spanish. Keep it in content or locale files (for example locales/es.json), separate from code.
- Use the terms in docs/glossary.md. It maps English terms to the owner's words.

## Layout
- `src/`: Source of the site or app.
- `assets/`: Static media used by the site.
- `tests/`: Automated tests.
- `scripts/`: Developer scripts. Optional.
- `docs/`: goals, glossary, assumptions, decisions and specs.
- `worker/`: part with the software profile. Read `worker/AGENTS.md` before working there.
- Files created by the official tool of a language or framework are allowed where the tool puts them. Declare any other top-level folder in .standard.yml under extra_folders, with a reason.

## Fixed rules
- Keep the top-level layout listed above. A new top-level folder is a yellow change.
- Only standard files and tool manifests live at the repository root. Everything else goes into a folder of the layout.
- Every top-level folder has a README.md saying what goes there, what does not and how files are named.
- Commit small, focused changes with Conventional Commits messages (feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore).
- Never commit secrets, tokens, personal data, executables, or files over 5 MB outside Git LFS.
- Leave the repository passing the standard check.
- Meet WCAG 2.2 AA. Text contrast of at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text), full keyboard use, visible focus, a label on every field, alt text on every meaningful image.
- Use native semantic HTML first (button, a, nav, main, headings in order). Every page has lang and a title.
- Every interactive element has hover, focus, active and disabled states. Async actions show loading, success and error.
- Every view that loads or lists data has empty, loading and error states.
- Layouts work from 320 px wide to large screens with no horizontal scroll.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
- Give images and embeds a width and height so nothing jumps while loading. Measure Core Web Vitals before claiming performance (LCP under 2.5 s, INP under 200 ms, CLS under 0.1).
- No fabricated content. No invented statistics, testimonials, logos, or links to pages that do not exist. Label honest placeholders as placeholders.
- No control without real behavior.
- Visual direction comes from DESIGN.md, written by the owner. Without it, label the work as a draft.

## Rules from this repository's options
- hosting = github-pages: Deploy with .github/workflows/pages.yml. In the repository settings, set the Pages source to GitHub Actions.
- build = none: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript served from src/. No bundler.
- motion = subtle: Animate only for feedback or continuity, 150 to 300 ms, using transform and opacity.
- three_d = none: Do not add 3D or WebGL.
- theme = both: Follow prefers-color-scheme and offer a toggle. Both themes meet the contrast rule.

## Allowed only with a written reason
Write the reason in docs/decisions/ before using any of these:
- Gradients, glows, glass effects or heavy shadows.
- 3D, parallax or scroll-driven animation.
- Decorative illustrations, or an icon set chosen for its look.
- More than two font families.
- Third-party scripts (analytics, widgets, embeds, trackers).

## Design patterns
- No pattern without a named, concrete problem and a decision record in docs/decisions/.
- Write the direct solution first. Add a pattern when the same problem shows up again.
- Patterns that fit this profile: state, observer, facade. Cards: https://github.com/SVN11X/standards/tree/v1/patterns

## Avoid AI slop
- No comments that restate the code, narrate steps or decorate (banners, emoji).
- No speculative abstractions, dead code, unused dependencies or leftover placeholder data.
- No fabricated content. Statistics, testimonials, references and links must be real and verified.
- No marketing words (seamless, cutting-edge, revolutionary, game-changer, supercharge).
- Plain prose. Short sentences, no filler openers, no em dashes or semicolons as separators.

## Owner preferences
- Use plain words. Explain a technical term briefly the first time it appears.
- Do not use em dashes or semicolons as separators. Use periods and commas.
- Reply in the language the owner writes in. Write every repository artifact in English.
